'''Bion of Abdera''' (c. 430 – 370 BC)<ref name="xanthi">{{citation|first=Αικατερίνη|last=Μπάλλα|author-link=|title=Βίων - από την Αικατερίνη Μπάλλα, Οδηγός Ανατολικής Μακεδονίας και Θράκης|publisher=|year=2007|location=|url=http://www.xanthi.ilsp.gr/cultureportalweb/article.php?article_id=937&topic_id=14&level=&belongs=&area_id=1&lang=gr}}</ref> ({{langx|el|Βίων ὁ Ἀβδηρίτης}}, ''gen.'' Βίωνος) was a [[Ancient Greece|Greek]] [[mathematician]] and [[astronomer]] of [[Abdera, Thrace]], and a pupil of [[Democritus]]. [[Strabo]] refers to him as an astrologer. <ref>Strabo, Geography, 1.2.21.</ref> He wrote both in the [[Ionic Greek|Ionic]] and [[Attic Greek|Attic]] dialects, and was the first who said that there were some parts of the Earth in which it was [[polar night|night for six months]], while the [[midnight sun|remaining six months]] were one uninterrupted day.<ref>Diogenes Laertius, IV.58.</ref><ref>Smith, William. ''Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology'' (1870), "Bion of Abdera".</ref> He also engaged in correlating the direction of [[winds]] with [[climate]] and is believed to have traveled to distant regions. <ref>Balla, p. 115</ref>
